title: Granular batching and fallback experiment log
content:
Purpose:

This is the lab-style experiment log for a customer-facing POC where the primary objective was to: reduce tail latency and per-token cost for short-chat interactions while preserving answer quality for high-precision prompts. The engagement prioritized: (1) per-request latency SLO of 120ms p50 for 64-token responses, (2) predictable cost envelope (<= 0.6x baseline tokens cost), and (3) no measurable regression on a 50-example prompt set (fidelity threshold: BLEU/ROUGE-like ad-hoc scoring and a small human QA panel).

Customer context:
- Customer: fintech chatbot (KYC support + policy explanations).
- Typical payload: short conversational turns, many single-shot clarifications, ~20–80 tokens outputs.
- Privacy: data routed through Redwood Dedicated; logs available for telemetry.
- Deployment: Dedicated pool (8x A10G equivalent) with autoscale bursts.

Constraints and guardrails:
- No model weight modifications allowed on customer's side. Only inference-time knobs: quantization variants we ship, routing policies, batching configuration, KV caching, and prompt-side heuristics.
- Must support graceful degradation if dedicated pool saturated (fallback to hosted-compat model variants).

Primary experiments run (lab-style notes):
1) Micro-batching cadence sweep (no KV cache)
   - Hypothesis: Very small batching window (1–8ms) improves throughput without increasing p50 by much due to request coalescing on the same GPU.
   - Variants: immediate flush (0ms), 4ms, 8ms; batch size cap 16
   - Models: rw-13b-v1 fp16, rw-13b-v1 int8-fp16-kernel (our quant profile), rw-7b-v2 fp16
   - Telemetry: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, gpu-util, compute-ms-per-token, quality checks (50 sample set)
   - Quick result: 4ms window with int8 profile gave best cost/latency tradeoff for rw-13b-v1 (p50 ~130ms -> still slightly over SLO); immediate flush had worst throughput.

2) Prefix KV caching (session-level) + batching sweep
   - Hypothesis: For multi-turn flows, prefix caching reduces compute significantly for repeated contexts. Cache hit ratio sensitivity to user session timeout examined.
   - Policy variants: per-session TTL 30s / 120s / sticky (session bound to worker)
   - Result: TTL 120s + 4ms batch window -> p50 110ms on rw-7b-v2 int8, cost ~0.55x baseline. However p95 degraded in bursty arrival patterns because cache priming created uneven load spikes.

3) Hybrid routing with fallback candidate pool
   - Design: Route by policy: low-latency tier (rw-7b-v2 int8) vs high-fidelity tier (rw-13b-v1 fp16). When low-tier queue depth > 6, route to mid-tier (rw-13b-v1 int8) and if dedicated pool saturated, route to hosted fallback (rw-7b-hosted-compat).
   - Observations: Smart routing reduced observed 502 errors during stress tests and kept p50 within target but raised median cost by ~7% due to occasional mid-tier fallbacks.

4) Aggressive quantization stress test (int4 / group-quant) on variant models
   - Noted that some customer prompts with numeric policy excerpts lose fidelity under int4 for rw-13b. Human QA flagged hallucination-like shifts in quoted policy snippets.
   - Decision: Disable int4 for any prompts containing 'policy' or 'terms' tokens via prompt tag detection.

Prompt and pipeline tuning experiments (quick notes):
- Prompt-slimming: Remove redundant framing and rely on conversation state stored in prefix KV cache -> average token reduction 12% per response.
- Context window trimming heuristic: dynamic-k (retain top-k most recent user turns where k=ceil(0.5*last_n)) gave better quality than fixed-turn cutoff for this workload.
- Output length caps: enforce max_tokens=96 for short clarifications; reduces p99 tails when combined with batch scheduling.

Measurement artifacts (snippet):
- Representative run (mixed traffic synthetic):
  Model: rw-7b-v2 int8, batch_window=4ms, KV-TTL=120s
  p50: 110ms, p95: 280ms, p99: 720ms
  Cost per 1000 requests: 0.56x baseline (baseline = rw-13b fp16 immediate-flush)
  Cache hit ratio: 42% (session length median 3 turns)
  Human QA pass rate: 47/50 (issues: 2 slightly truncated policy citations, 1 missing nuance)

Key analysis and tradeoffs:
- Batching window: sweet spot ~3–6ms for our hardware cluster. Too long increases p50; too short kills throughput. Variance depends on request arrival distribution (bursty vs Poisson).
- KV cache: large wins for multi-turn, but priming burden causes p95 spikes. Consider background priming or staggered cache warming.
- Quantization: int8 offered predictable cost/latency gains without major fidelity drop on our test set; int4 introduced pathologies on numeric/legal text and must be gated.
- Hybrid routing: excellent for reliability; complexity increases telemetry needs (per-route quality metrics) and billing nuances.

Decisions made for the customer POC (proposal to customer):
1) Default: rw-7b-v2 int8 on low-latency tier with 4ms batch window + KV-TTL 120s for active users.
2) High-precision routes: rw-13b-v1 fp16 for flagged admin/policy flows (explicit API route).
3) Fallback policy: hosted-compat rw-7b-hosted if dedicated pool triggers saturation; circuit-breaker per-region.
4) Disable int4 for any prompt containing tokens in the "policy/terms/numeric" tag list.
5) Instrument new per-route quality signals (flagged_mismatch, hallucination_score) and add to Console dashboard.

Checklist for handoff to customer's SRE / Redwood Dedicated ops team:
- [ ] Apply batch_window=4ms in production config template for customer pool
- [ ] Add route-level QoS metrics to Console: p50/p95/p99, cost-per-1k, cache-hit-ratio, route-fallback-count
- [ ] Implement prompt tag detector plugin and int4 gating rule
- [ ] Create a canary rollout: 10% users -> 50% -> 100% over 48h with rollback automation
- [ ] Create runbook entries for cache-priming overload and fallback runaway (include thresholds: queue_depth>12 for 30s triggers failover)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How to smooth cache priming spikes without global throttling? Options: staggered background priming, soft-deprioritization, or adaptive TTL per session based on recent QPS.
- Should we invest engineering cycles in a lightweight on-worker prefetcher for popular prompts? Estimate: 2–3 sprint effort.
- Billing clarity: how to present hybrid-routing costs to the customer (blended vs pass-through)? Needs finance + GTM decision.
- Telemetry: need to instrument prompt-tag correlation with fidelity drops and automatically surface possible int4-regressed prompts.

Run-level notes (time-stamped):
- 2024-11-03 09:20: initial micro-batching sweep, queue-based synthetic load
- 2024-11-04 14:32: KV-TTL 30s test; noticed cache churn and low hit ratio (18%).
- 2024-11-06 11:10: int4 stress test; 3/50 human QA failures for numeric extraction prompts.
- 2024-11-10 16:40: Hybrid routing prototype implemented; 502s eliminated during saturation test.
- 2024-11-12 09:05: Final validation sweep with customer dataset subset (not full production) -> propose RW-7B int8 as default.

Appendix: short snippets to reproduce key experiments locally:
- Start test harness: python se_lab/harness.py --model rw-7b-v2 --quant int8 --batch-window 4 --kv-ttl 120 --arrival=poisson
- Metrics export: curl http://ops-metrics.local/metrics?run=lab-20241110 > lab-20241110.json

Contact / owners for follow-ups: Nina Patel (SE lead) nina@redwood.ai, Oscar Ruiz (infrastructure), Jae Kim (quantization lead).

Notes to self: prioritize telemetry for per-prompt quality signals before enabling any more aggressive quant profiles. Add quick automated human-in-the-loop check for policy-like prompt classes.

End of log.
